quick_guide.text: Check that the tow vehicle's hitch ball is 2-5/16 inches and rated for at least 14,000 lb, and that the ball, hitch and coupler have no cracks, wear or looseness.

source_refs.locator: p. 6, 1.2.4 warning; pp. 41-43, "Trailer with Ball-Hitch Coupler"

quick_guide.text: Lower the coupler fully onto the ball, close the latch and put the pin or lock through it. Test it: raise the rear of the tow vehicle 1 inch with the trailer jack (no more), then lower and raise the jack fully.

source_refs.locator: p. 43, "Prepare the coupler and hitch"; p. 44, "Couple the trailer to the tow vehicle"

quick_guide.text: Cross the safety chains under the coupler and hook them to the tow vehicle's frame with the S-hooks put in from underneath; slack to turn, not to drag.

Clip the breakaway cable to the tow vehicle (not to a chain or the hitch) so it pulls before the chains go tight. Test it: pull the pin and try to pull the trailer forward; you should feel the brakes. Put the pin straight back.

source_refs.locator: p. 8, 1.2.6; pp. 45-46, "Attach and test electric breakaway brake system"

quick_guide.text: Connect the 7-way plug and check the tail, brake and turn lights. Then, moving at under 5 mph, apply the brake controller by hand and feel the trailer brakes work.
Look for tire damage, set the pressure printed on the VIN label (front left) while the tires are cold, and check that the lug nuts are tight.

Load with the trailer hitched and on level ground. Stay within the payload on the trailer's decal (listed cargo capacity 9,820 lb). Spread loose material evenly front to back and side to side; secure anything that is not loose material.
Before dumping: trailer level and on firm ground, area clear of people, no power lines overhead. Open the rear doors and chain them to the sides, then open the control box.

source_refs.locator: p. 63, danger box; p. 64, 4.4.6; p. 67, power-line warning

quick_guide.text: Standing well clear, hold UP until the body is about halfway up, then stop and check behind the trailer for room. Raise to about three-quarters and check again. Never leave the controls while the body is up.
If the load sticks, do not jerk the button or brake hard to shake it loose. Lower the body and free the load by hand.
When empty: lower the body fully, close and latch the doors, and lock the hoist controls before you move.
Every 50 miles or hour of towing, stop and check the coupler, chains, load and doors.
To unhitch: block the tires, unplug, unclip the breakaway cable, unhook the chains, open the coupler, check the ground under the jack, then lower the jack to take the tongue weight.

source_refs.locator: p. 47, "Uncoupling the Ball Hitch Trailer with Tongue Jack"

warnings.text: Never go under a raised dump body. The body prop is for maintenance and holds an empty body only.
If the hoist will not lift the load, unload some by hand. Never help the hoist with a jack, crane or other machine.
Do not fully raise a loaded body: the tow vehicle's rear wheels can lose traction.
A raised body near power lines can electrocute without touching them. Check overhead before raising.
Do not move the trailer until the coupler is locked, the chains and breakaway cable are attached and the jack is fully raised.
Never carry people, or flammable, explosive or poisonous materials.
60 mph is the maximum recommended towing speed, and only in ideal conditions.

support_notes.text: "The box won't go up" with the pump only clicking or silent: the hoist manual's first check is that the battery is fully charged.
support_notes.status_reason: The Hoist Manual does not list the 14LP; Big Tex has not confirmed it applies.

support_notes.text: Loaded body will not rise all the way: the hoist manual says to check all electrical connections (ground and positive) are tight.
Empty body will not rise all the way: the hoist manual says to check the reservoir fluid with the bed down (1 inch from the top). Hydraulic work goes to a qualified technician.
Hoist will not lift the load: reduce the load by hand and get service from a qualified hydraulics technician. Never assist the hoist.

Lights or brakes dead: check the 7-way connection (an improper connection leaves the lights and electric brakes inoperable). Staff can compare the contacts with Big Tex's 7-way RV sheet; the two Big Tex sheets label the black and blue wires differently, so confirm on the trailer.
Breakaway test fails: do not tow until the brakes or the breakaway battery are repaired. The battery runs down fast while the pin is out.

headline.text: 14 ft tandem-axle dump trailer with electric brakes, breakaway and a battery-powered hoist. It tows on a 2-5/16 inch ball rated for 14,000 lb or more, with a brake controller in the truck.
headline.status_reason: Facts from the OEM product page and the dump-trailer manual.

quick_start_text.text:
1. Ball: 2-5/16 inch, rated 14,000 lb or more. Seat the coupler, latch it and pin it.
2. Lift-test: raise the truck 1 inch with the jack (no more), then raise the jack fully.
3. Cross the safety chains under the coupler and hook them to the truck's frame.
4. Clip the breakaway cable to the truck, not to a chain. Test: pull the pin, feel the brakes hold, put the pin straight back.
5. Plug in the 7-way and check the lights. Then, under 5 mph, apply the brake controller and feel the trailer brakes.
6. Tires: no damage, pressure as printed on the VIN label (front left), lug nuts tight.
7. Load hitched and level, within the payload decal (9,820 lb listed). Spread loose material evenly.
8. To dump: level, firm ground, people clear, no power lines overhead. Chain the doors open, raise in stages and check behind.
The Start-Up Guide shows each step.
quick_start_text.status_reason: Condensed from sourced steps; awaiting the reviewer.

safety_notes.text:
Never go under a raised dump body. The body prop is for maintenance, with the body empty.
Stay at the controls while the body is up. Lower it fully, latch the doors and lock the controls before you move.
Don't fully raise a loaded body: the truck's rear wheels can lose traction.
If the hoist won't lift the load, unload some by hand. Never push it with a jack or machine.
A raised body near power lines can electrocute without touching them.
Don't move until the coupler is locked, the chains and breakaway cable are on and the jack is up. 60 mph is the maximum recommended speed, in ideal conditions only. No people or hazardous loads.
safety_notes.status_reason: Condensed from sourced warnings; awaiting the reviewer.

fuel_power_notes.text:
The hoist runs on the trailer's 12 V deep-cycle battery, which has an onboard 110 V charger and a 5 W solar charger.
The breakaway battery runs down fast while its pin is out, so put the pin straight back after testing.
fuel_power_notes.status_reason: Battery facts from the product page; the pin line from the manual; awaiting the reviewer.

troubleshooting_notes.text:
Hoist won't lift the load: unload some by hand, then use Request Support. Never push it with a jack or machine.
Load stuck: lower the body and free it by hand. Don't jerk the button or brake hard.
Lights or brakes dead: check the 7-way plug is fully connected.
Breakaway test fails: don't tow. Use Request Support.
troubleshooting_notes.status_reason: Condensed from sourced notes; the hoist manual's battery check stays off the page until Big Tex confirms it applies.

return_notes.text:
Return the straps, chain pins, spare tire and the hoist remote.
Body fully down, doors latched, controls locked.
To unhitch: block the tires, unplug, unclip the breakaway cable, unhook the chains, open the coupler, then lower the jack on firm ground.
Use Return checklist when you drop it off.
